requirements.requirement: node1 configured as writable PostgreSQL streaming-replication primary (wal_level, replication slots, replicator role)
requirements.summary: postgresql.conf set listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on; pg_hba.conf opened scram-sha-256 replication/app auth for the cluster subnet; service started active; replicator role created; appdb/demo table with baseline rows created and confirmed writable (pg_is_in_recovery=f after restart).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys streaming from node1
requirements.summary: pg_basebackup -R against node1 succeeded on both nodes producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing at node1; firewall opened for postgresql; service started active on both; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both streaming async.

requirements.requirement: Standbys are read-only (reject writes) and in recovery
requirements.summary: pg_is_in_recovery()=t on node2 and node3; direct INSERT attempt on node2 fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
requirements.summary: An insert on node1 ('post-replication-check') appeared on both node2 and node3 after a 1s wait; re-verified post-restart with a second insert ('post-restart-check') visible on both standbys.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 636556ce and healthy standby/data state captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; boot_id changed to b12b662d (matches after_executor lifecycle snapshot); postgresql active, still in recovery, row count intact, primary shows node2 reconnected streaming.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node3 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 7ef78016 captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to af9a0f07 (matches after_executor snapshot); postgresql active, in recovery, row count intact, primary shows node3 reconnected streaming.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 (primary) healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered writable state and reconnected standbys
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2b19e976 captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 984814e2 (matches after_executor snapshot); postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=f (still primary/writable), row count intact, both standbys reconnected/streaming.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the streaming replication contract: node1 is a writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only async standbys built via pg_basebackup -R, replication was verified live in both directions (writes propagate, standby writes rejected), and this was re-confirmed after a complete, evidence-rich one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes (standbys first, then primary), each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a changed boot identity cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full service/data/cluster recovery. No task requirements were left unmet.
limitations: Some /tmp log files (pg_install*.log, reboot.log) were left behind on all nodes as minor residue from the install/reboot process; low severity, no functional impact.

Replicator role password was passed via secret_env and redacted in captured output, so its value cannot be independently verified, though role creation and successful authenticated pg_basebackup connections confirm it worked.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were closely tied to the task: install attempts failed transiently due to a repo GPG parsing race (diagnosed with read-only commands sha256sum/gpg --show-keys, then resolved by clearing the dnf cache and retrying — cmd-10d82c0f3f034a9b), a legitimate corrective step with a clear causal link to completing the install, not an unnecessary mutation. Wiping node2/node3 data directories before pg_basebackup (cmd-a8550d77c74549ba, cmd-05a9c6e905b942a5) was a necessary prerequisite for standby setup on freshly initialized but unused data dirs. Firewalld changes (cmd-6e9b15ad08f2486b, cmd-2974497c9a3a4cc2, cmd-768775d2b7b64d89) were narrowly scoped (postgresql service only) and required for replication traffic. Minor residue: several install/reboot log files (/tmp/pg_install*.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left on all three nodes per the after_executor snapshot diff — low-risk, non-destructive leftover files with no functional impact.
